title: Trafalgar, 1805 — Nelson's last signal, and the barrel of brandy
sources: Wikipedia: Battle of Trafalgar — 21 October 1805; Nelson's fleet of 27 ships of the line against Villeneuve's 33; Nelson sailed at the allied line in two columns to break it; 18 allied ships were captured or destroyed while the British lost none; Victory locked masts with Redoutable, and a musket ball fired from Redoutable's mizzentop struck Nelson in the left shoulder and lodged near his spine; at 11:45 Nelson sent the signal 'England expects that every man will do his duty'

Wikipedia: England expects that every man will do his duty — Nelson asked signal officer Pasco to signal 'England confides that every man will do his duty'; Pasco suggested 'expects', which was in the signal vocabulary, while 'confides' had to be spelt out; Nelson agreed

Wikipedia: Horatio Nelson, 1st Viscount Nelson — surgeon Beatty heard him murmur 'Thank God I have done my duty'; he died at half past four, three hours after being hit; his body was preserved in a cask of brandy mixed with camphor and myrrh for the trip home to a grand state funeral
Also on this day (candidates.md, in the app): 1854 Florence Nightingale and 38 nurses are sent to the Crimean War; 1959 the Guggenheim Museum opens in New York

post.facebook:
On this day in 1805, Horatio Nelson's fleet met the combined French and Spanish fleets off Cape Trafalgar.

Nelson had 27 ships of the line against 33. Instead of forming a line of battle, he drove into the enemy's line in two columns to break it apart. Before the fighting he asked for a signal: "England confides that every man will do his duty." His signal officer suggested "expects" — it was in the code book, while "confides" would have to be spelt out letter by letter. Nelson agreed.

As HMS Victory fought the French Redoutable, a musket ball from her rigging struck Nelson in the shoulder and lodged near his spine. Eighteen allied ships were captured or destroyed; the British lost none. Below deck, the surgeon heard Nelson murmur, "Thank God I have done my duty." He died three hours after he was hit — and his body was kept in a cask of brandy for the voyage home to a state funeral.

Also on 21 October: Florence Nightingale set off for the Crimean War (1854), and the Guggenheim Museum opened (1959).

youtube.description:
21 October 1805 — the Battle of Trafalgar. Horatio Nelson's 27 ships faced 33 French and Spanish ships and broke their line in two columns. His famous signal almost read "England confides that every man will do his duty" — until his signal officer suggested "expects", a word already in the code book. Eighteen enemy ships were captured or destroyed and Britain lost none, but a French musket ball killed Nelson. "Thank God I have done my duty." His body came home in a cask of brandy.

Also on 21 October: Florence Nightingale sets off for Crimea (1854) and the Guggenheim Museum opens (1959).
